name: Mississippi
overview: Mississippi sells tax liens, not the land itself, on property with unpaid ad valorem taxes. Each county tax collector holds an annual tax sale under Mississippi Code Sections 27-41-49 to 27-41-89; DeSoto County says that, like most counties, it holds the sale on the last Monday in August each year. Several large counties, including DeSoto and Jackson, now run the sale online through GovEase. After the sale the owner has two years from the purchase date to redeem by paying the taxes plus interest of 1.5% per month; if the property is not redeemed within two years, the purchaser can acquire it. Each year the county chancery clerks send the Secretary of State a list of property whose taxes went unpaid and whose owner did not redeem in time, and those properties go into the state's tax-forfeited inventory for sale.

counties.how_to_bid: Register online with GovEase (registration opened August 3rd for the 2026 sale) and take its free online training. All deposits are made through GovEase; no deposits are taken at county offices, and credit card transactions carry a convenience fee. Bidders can enter maximum bids ahead of time; the sale usually lasts five to seven days. Taxes not paid by the last Friday before the sale are auctioned. If the owner redeems within two years, the purchaser is repaid the lien amount plus 1.5% per month interest (not on the overbid); end-of-sale processing goes through the Chancery Clerk.

counties.how_to_bid: Sign up and register online with GovEase; online registration begins the first week of August, and free web training is offered. Bidders can enter maximum bids ahead of time; the sale usually lasts five to seven days and runs until all delinquent parcels are sold. Taxes not paid by the last Friday before the sale are auctioned. Accepted payment: company or personal check (with bank letter), cashier's check or money order. Deposit not stated.
